title: Grill round 3: replacing prUrl with a list, and Create all PRs on single-repo tasks
summary: Round 2 is complete. You chose to **replace `prUrl` with a list everywhere** and to **show Create all PRs on single-repo tasks** with more than one proposal. Both are bigger than what I'd recommended. Here are the 4 decisions they force, plus 3 defaults to confirm. After this the record is complete.
proven: **Who reads `prUrl` today.** In the core: `db.ts`, `server.ts` (stamping), `orchestrator.ts`/`pipeline-runner.ts` (initialize to null), `task-repos.ts`. In the webview: `RunPanel`, `App.tsx` (View PR), `task-context-menu.ts`, `pr-url.ts`, `commit-push.ts`, `multi-repo-ui.ts`, `repo-removal.ts`, `pr-proposal.ts`, `api.ts`. Shared: `types.ts`, `multi-repo.ts`. The e2e spec reads it too.

**The CLI and TUI never read `prUrl`.** Only test fixtures set it to null. The Companion app has no routes yet (`security.md`), so no client outside this repo reads it today. The one external surface is the Task JSON that `GET /tasks` and `agetor ls --json` print.
Storage today: `tasks.pr_url` (migration 031, single-repo) and `repositories[].prUrl` inside the `repositories` JSON (migration 091, multi-repo).

sections.title: Replacing `prUrl` with a list
sections.intro: Your round-2 answer: **"Replace `prUrl` with a list everywhere."** These settle what that means for stored data and the Task JSON.

questions.title: Migration 092 copies each single-repo task's `pr_url` into the new list. What happens to the old `tasks.pr_url` column?
questions.why: Dropping a column is one-way (like migration 072). If you ever run an older build against the migrated DB, it can't open it.
questions.context:
Multi-repo entries are JSON, so `repositories[].prUrl` → `repositories[].prs` is a read-time conversion plus a rewrite on the next write, with no column change.

For `tasks.pr_url`, 092 adds a `prs` JSON column (server-managed) and backfills it.

options.label: Keep the column, stop reading and writing it
options.consequence: Reversible. An older build would still see the PR it stamped before the upgrade, but none created after.

options.label: Keep the column and mirror the first PR into it on each stamp (never read)
options.consequence: Reversible, and an older build sees the first PR. One extra write, which is a compatibility shim inside "replace everywhere".

options.label: Drop it (`ALTER TABLE … DROP COLUMN`)
options.consequence: Cleanest, and one-way. Downgrading requires restoring a backup.

recommendation.reason: It keeps the DB downgrade-safe at no cost, and no code in this repo reads the column any more, so the replace is still complete.

questions.title: The Task JSON (`GET /tasks`, `agetor ls --json`): what happens to the `prUrl` field?
questions.why: It's the only part of this change visible outside the repo: scripts that parse `agetor ls --json`, and the future Companion.

options.label: Remove `prUrl`; only `prs` remains (on the task and on each repository)
options.consequence: One shape everywhere. A script reading `.prUrl` silently gets `undefined`.

options.label: Add `prs`; keep `prUrl` as a deprecated, derived read-only field (the first PR's URL), never read by agetor itself
options.consequence: External readers keep working. The code still has one source of truth (`prs`).

recommendation.reason: No known consumer reads it, and you asked for the list everywhere. Keeping a derived copy is exactly the half-replacement you rejected.

recommendation.value: `{ url: string, head: string, base: string, number: number | null, createdAt: number }`, in creation order. A repository's (or single-repo task's) **live-head PR** is the one whose `head` matches its branch, not just the first item.
recommendation.reason: `head` drives duplicate skipping, `base` is shown in the run panel, and `number` saves re-parsing the URL for View PR.

questions.title: On a single-repo task, when does Create all PRs appear?
questions.why: Your round-2 answer: **"show Create all PRs … on single-repo tasks with more than one proposal."** This pins down "more than one".

options.label: When the newest matching proposals name **two or more distinct heads** that don't have a PR yet; shown next to the existing Create PR chip
options.consequence: The chip stays the one-PR path into the composer. Create all PRs appears only when there's really more than one.

options.label: When the reply has two or more proposals, even for the same head
options.consequence: It can appear for duplicate proposals of one PR.

options.label: Always on single-repo tasks, replacing the Create PR chip
options.consequence: One flow, but the composer path (edit the body with full formatting) loses its entry point.

recommendation.reason: It's the case you asked for and nothing else, and the familiar chip keeps working.

questions.title: "View PR" (run panel link, task card, right-click menu) when a task or repository has several PRs?

options.label: List them all: the run panel shows each `head → base` link; the context menu gets one "View PR: <head>" item per PR (a submenu past 3)
options.consequence: Every PR stays reachable from where you look today.

options.label: Show only the live-head PR, as today; extra PRs only in the run panel
options.consequence: Less UI, but extra PRs are hidden from the card and the menu.

recommendation.reason: "Replace everywhere" means every reader handles the list, and a PR you can't find after creating it is a bug report waiting to happen.

questions.title: Server-managed rules for the new columns

recommendation.value: `tasks.base_branch` and `tasks.prs` are server-managed (not in `ALLOWED_PATCH_FIELDS`, skipped by the generic SET, never bump `updated_at`, written by targeted UPDATEs). Both go in migration 092, and the CLAUDE.md list is updated.
recommendation.reason: CLAUDE.md requires it for every server-written column.

recommendation.value: A new step's task-level `prs` starts empty (as `prUrl: null` does today, `pipeline-runner.ts:1441`). Its `baseBranch` is copied from the parent like `baseRef` (`:1434`). Its `repositories[]`, each entry's `prs` and `baseBranch` included, are copied from the parent as they are today (`:1437`).
recommendation.reason: That's exactly how the step copies the parent's state today, with the new fields following the old ones.
